newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria says currency board possible end February.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria says currency board possible end February.

text.p: Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said on Tuesday Bulgaria will be able to introduce a currency board plan by the end of February if technical preparations are speeded up.
"By the end of February we may be ready to introduce currency board rules if the technical preparations, which must be speeded up, are completed," Kostov told a news conference.

Kostov said technical preparations included amendments to the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) law which would lay out key rules for its future operations, due to be approved first by the cabinet and then by parliament.

The BNB will be reduced to four departments which include an Issue Department, which will control the currency board, a Banking department, a Bank Supervsion Department and a Debt Management unit, Kostov said.
"Bulgaria will retain its central bank as an insititution, which will act in line with currency board rules and not be banned from independent monetary policy," Kostov said.
Under a currency board system the levs in circulation must be matched by the foreign exchange reserves and central bank lending to the government and commercial banks is curbed.

Kostov said that a seven-member board which includes a central bank governor, three deputy governors and three independent experts will replace the current nine-member board and a numerous plenary council.
All of the central bank board members should be proposed by the president and approved by parliament, said Kostov.

Under an alternative proposal, which will be also submitted to parliament for approval, central bank governor and his deputies could be elected by parliament and the three independent experts appointed by the President.
The central bank issue department will be expected to publish information on the reserve currency and covered monetary base on weekly basis.
Bulgaria is also due to amend its regulations on bank bankruptcy and court procedures, Kostov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
